units.title: A positive strongly convex potential attains its minimum
units.boundary: This is a finite-dimensional existence and first-order optimality theorem. It does not normalize a Gibbs law, prove concentration, or construct a sampling algorithm.

sources.label: Smoothed Picard Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, Lemma 4.16 proof, PDF p.22
sources.scope: ASTIS expands the omitted existence justification for the minimizer selected in the proof.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
V is genuinely differentiable on all of E.
V is strongly convex on all of E with strictly positive modulus m.
units.statement: There is a point p that minimizes V globally, and the genuine gradient of V vanishes at p.
units.formula: \exists p\in E:\quad V(p)\le V(x)\ \forall x\in E,\qquad \nabla V(p)=0.

steps.title: Expose quadratic growth
steps.text: Apply the compiled first-order model at the origin. The linear gradient term is the only possible negative contribution.
steps.lean: StrongConvexFirstOrder.firstOrder_lower_bound_of_strongConvexOn supplies the inequality from genuine differentiability.

steps.title: Choose a compact search ball
steps.text: Cauchy-Schwarz shows that outside radius two times the origin-gradient norm divided by m, the quadratic term absorbs the linear term.
steps.lean: abs_real_inner_le_norm and positivity justify the comparison without dividing by a possibly zero norm.

steps.title: Attain the global minimum
steps.text: The closed ball of radius R is compact in finite dimension. Continuity gives a minimizer p in the ball. Its value is no larger than V(0), while every point outside has value at least V(0), so p is globally minimizing.
steps.formula: p\in\overline B(0,R),\quad V(p)\le V(0)\le V(x)\quad(x\notin\overline B(0,R)).
steps.lean: isCompact_closedBall.exists_isMinOn supplies p; a ball-membership split promotes the restricted minimum to Set.univ.

steps.title: Use Fermat's theorem
steps.text: A differentiable function has zero derivative at a local minimum; in an inner-product space this is exactly zero gradient.
steps.lean: IsLocalMin.fderiv_eq_zero closes the genuine first-order condition.

units.lean_statement: The theorem requires positive modulus and finite dimension. It uses Differentiable rather than a totalized fderiv equality as its regularity witness.
units.lean_proof: The Lean proof implements the coercive-ball argument directly, reusing the ASTIS first-order strong-convexity theorem and Mathlib compactness/Fermat APIs.

units.title: The SPHMC q=2 initialization bound with no supplied critical point
units.boundary: This closes the minimizer-existence gap in the q=2 component of Lemma 4.16. The source's q>2 concentration, the Picard kernel, final accuracy and query complexity are still not proved.

sources.label: Smoothed Picard Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, Lemma 4.16, PDF p.22
sources.scope: The source selects a minimizer internally; ASTIS now constructs it from the printed curvature assumptions.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space.
U is C2 with alpha I <= Hessian U <= I and 0 < alpha <= 1.
The reference point has squared gradient norm at most alpha times dimension.
The smoothing variance eta lies in [0,1].
units.statement: For the actual normalized Gibbs law, its Gaussian smoothing and standard-Gaussian momentum, the q=2 squared M-kappa transport initialization cost is at most 5 kappa d, with the minimizer derived rather than assumed.

steps.title: Convert Hessian curvature to strong convexity
steps.text: The genuine C2 Hessian lower bound implies whole-space strong convexity with the same alpha.

steps.title: Construct the source minimizer
steps.text: Positive strong convexity and differentiability supply a global minimizer p with zero gradient; p is not added as a theorem hypothesis.

steps.title: Apply the verified numerical transport chain
steps.text: The constructed critical point is fed to the already verified Gibbs moment, smoothing and identical-momentum coupling theorem.
steps.lean: InitialGibbsPhaseTransport.initial_gibbs_phase_transport_q2 supplies the actual normalized measures and constant.

units.lean_statement: The formal statement has exactly the previous q=2 conclusion but no p parameter or gradient-zero premise. Coordinate-free finite-dimensional E and eta=0 remain valid generalizations.
units.lean_proof: The proof composes the genuine Hessian-to-strong-convexity bridge, the new minimizer theorem and the independently verified conditional q=2 theorem.
